description: Four-panel TEM group (bright-field micrographs, all with 500 nm scale bars) comparing the deformation substructure of annealed 0Cr and 6Cr low-density steel strips at a true strain of 0.075. (a) 0Cr strip: a dashed yellow line marks a "Slip band", a double-headed arrow along the {111} trace marks the slip plane, and a yellow arrow points to "Dislocation arrays"; an inset selected-area electron diffraction pattern is indexed to the [110] zone axis. (b) 0Cr strip: a typical dislocation network/tangle structure with dense cell-like walls and a dislocation-free region. (c) 6Cr strip: closely spaced, dark slip bands with a double-headed {111} arrow and an inset [110] SAED pattern. (d) 6Cr strip: scattered dislocations and localised entanglements/agglomerations between slip bands plus a heavily dark banded region. Comparing (a) with (c) shows the slip-band spacing is smaller in 6Cr than in 0Cr at the same strain; (b) and (d) show that 0Cr forms a dislocation network whereas 6Cr retains more scattered, entangled dislocations. No numeric values are printed; diffraction spot indices beyond the [110] zone-axis label are not annotated.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of annealed 0Cr steel strip at true strain 0.075, 500 nm scale bar. A dashed yellow line is labelled "Slip band", a double-headed yellow arrow is labelled "{111}", and a yellow arrow points to "Dislocation arrays". Inset SAED pattern labelled [110].
Bright-field TEM micrograph of 0Cr steel strip showing a typical dislocation network structure: dense tangled dislocation walls forming irregular cells, 500 nm scale bar.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of annealed 6Cr steel strip at true strain 0.075, 500 nm scale bar. Multiple closely spaced dark slip bands run diagonally, marked by a double-headed yellow arrow labelled "{111}". Inset SAED pattern labelled [110].

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 6Cr steel strip showing scattered, loosely distributed dislocations together with regions where dislocations between slip bands are entangled and agglomerated, and a darker banded area; 500 nm scale bar.

observations.observation: All four panels are bright-field TEM micrographs, each carrying a 500 nm scale bar.
Panel (a) shows a 0Cr steel strip with a dashed line annotated "Slip band", an arrow annotated "Dislocation arrays", and a double-headed arrow labelled "{111}" indicating the slip plane trace.
The insets in panels (a) and (c) are selected-area electron diffraction patterns labelled [110], appearing as regular spot arrays (single-crystal/near-single-crystal austenite).
Panel (b) shows a dislocation network structure in the 0Cr steel strip, with tangled dislocation walls and cell-like arrangements.
Panel (c) shows slip bands in the 6Cr steel strip that are more closely spaced than the slip band in the 0Cr panel (a).
Panel (d) shows scattered dislocations plus regions where dislocations between slip bands are entangled and agglomerated in the 6Cr steel strip.
The caption identifies the panels as (a) slip bands in 0Cr, (b) dislocation network structure in 0Cr, (c) slip bands in 6Cr, (d) scattered dislocations in 6Cr, all at a true strain of 0.075.
The citing text states that the addition of 6Cr makes the spacing of the slip bands smaller than that of 0Cr steel strips at this strain stage.

The citing text states that the higher density of slip bands caused by the same strain would result in a higher strain hardening rate in the 6Cr steel strips because it makes dislocation glide more difficult.
The citing text states the dislocation network structure in 0Cr austenite (b) is similar to that in austenite-ferrite Fe-18.1Mn-9.6Al-0.65C steel at a true strain of 0.06.
The citing text states that the slip bands and dislocation arrays in (a) and (c) indicate a typical planar slip characteristic.
No numeric values (spacing, density, strain) are printed on any panel; only the 500 nm scale bars and the {111}/[110] orientation labels are legible.
